edges.description: Reduced transketolase activity blocks recycling of pentose phosphates, causing accumulation of polyols and pentose(-ulose) phosphates.
Transketolase deficiency is proposed to reduce NADPH synthesis, limiting reductive biosynthesis and maintenance of cerebral glutathione.
intermediate_mechanisms: Diminished NADPH generation limiting glutathione-dependent redox defense.
edges.target: Reduced NADPH-dependent biosynthesis and redox defense

edges.description: Accumulated polyols and pentose(-ulose) phosphates are excreted, producing an abnormal urinary metabolite (polyol/sugar-phosphate) profile.
Impaired NADPH-dependent nucleic acid synthesis and cell division is proposed to underlie growth failure.
edges.source: Reduced NADPH-dependent biosynthesis and redox defense

edges.description: Reduced NADPH-dependent maintenance of cerebral glutathione is proposed to contribute to neurodevelopmental delay.
edges.source: Reduced NADPH-dependent biosynthesis and redox defense

nodes.description: Affected individuals excrete elevated amounts of the polyols erythritol, arabitol, and ribitol together with pentose(-ulose)-5-phosphates in urine, the diagnostic biochemical signature of transketolase deficiency.

nodes.description: Biallelic TKT variants reduce transketolase enzymatic activity. Enzymatic testing in affected individuals confirmed significantly reduced transketolase activity, establishing the primary catalytic defect in the non-oxidative branch of the pentose phosphate pathway.
